spec.title: codkit PROP-004: Markers and the .ckpatch patch format

status.comment: standalone marker and deterministic patch format contract

p.MARKER-CARRIES-ONLY-ID: A marker carries the identifier and nothing else; the full metadata live in the delta artifact in the patch set (the patch header and the like). This way the marker does not inflate the patch or the context of the diff, and it is carried over renames reliably, together with the metadata, by the identifier.

facts.MR-LINE-SHAPE: A marker line: an optional indent, the comment form, the word `codkit:begin|end`, one space, an id matching `idPattern`. Nothing else on the line (except the comment terminator for CSS/HTML).
facts.MR-ASCII-ONLY: Marker lines and the service comments inside a block use ASCII, so as not to introduce a dependency on a fork-specific Unicode hygiene policy.
facts.MR-FUNCTIONAL-ONLY: Inside a block: a functional change only; upstream lines that are neutralized are **commented out, not deleted**; formatting edits outside one's own block are forbidden; multi-line logic is not written where a one-line hook is enough - the logic lives in own code.
facts.MR-STABLE-ANCHOR: A hook is placed at a point of the particular pin that is stable: preferably the beginning of an existing `create*` method, not a constructor signature; DI goes through an accessor or instantiation service that is already available, not through a new constructor parameter.
facts.MR-NO-NESTING: Nesting of markers is forbidden; one id may cover blocks in several files only for the `entry-module` layer (PROP-005 §4), otherwise it is one file.
facts.MR-SEVERAL-BLOCKS-ONE-ID: One id may open **several blocks in one file**: a graft usually consists of an import line and a call site, and that is one intervention, not two. The blocks of one id are not nested inside each other; every block of the file with that id belongs to one artifact (`save` collects them into one patch, `verify` counts the graft budget over all the blocks together - PROP-005 `PATCH-HOOK-BUDGET`). `CK-E-MARKER-DUP-ID` remains the error of two *records* with one id and of a repeated `marker new` with an id already taken. Decision of 2026-09-07: before it the rule «one block per file» forced one either to put the import and the call site under different ids (two records about one intervention) or to stretch the block over the whole span between them; rejected - both variants lie to the inventory.
facts.MR-BLIND-ZONES: JSON without comments and binary files have no marker by construction - their interventions live in the overlay, the resource map or the removed registry, and must have a guard test.
facts.MR-FORM-KEY: The key of a file in `markerComment` is its extension - or, for a file whose name begins with a dot and carries no extension (`.vscodeignore`, `.gitignore`, `.npmignore`), its whole name, which `extname` reads as nameless; the shipped conventions give those three the `#` form (2026-11-01: the licence of an extension's distributable is stated through one line of its ignore file, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-019#GEN-LICENSING` (6)). Every reader and writer of markers keys a path through one function, so a file without a key has no form (`MR-BLIND-ZONES`) everywhere alike.

marker-parser.title: 3. Marker parsing (the algorithm)

p.parser-io: Input: the content of the file (bytes), the extension. Output: a list of blocks `{id, beginLine, endLine}` (1-based lines, the marker lines included) plus a list of errors.

p.PARSER-PERFORMANCE: Performance: a linear pass; the pre-commit requirement is a fraction of a second per file (PROP-012 §3).

patch-file.title: 4. A patch - the file delta/patches/*.ckpatch

p.PATCH-NAME-ENCODING: **The file name** encodes the path of the upstream file: the separator `/` is replaced by `__` (a double underscore), and the extension `.ckpatch` is appended to the full name. The patch of a file whose name begins with a dot (`.gitignore.ckpatch`, `MR-FORM-KEY`) therefore begins with a dot too: it is the one artifact name the engine writes that does, and the portable-name rule of the engine's file writer holds for the rest of its shape (2026-11-01). Example: `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/titlebar/titlebarPart.ts` → `delta/patches/src__vs__workbench__browser__parts__titlebar__titlebarPart.ts.ckpatch`. Decoding back: cut off `.ckpatch`, replace `__` with `/`. Before the replacement the encoder checks that the path contains no `__`, and on a collision it fails with code 2 (there are no such paths at the pin; the check is for the future).

p.PATCH-STRUCTURE: **The structure of the file**: the metadata header, then the unified diff. The header is the lines that start with `# `, up to the first `--- ` line; `git apply` ignores such lines (garbage before the diff headers), so the file is applicable as an ordinary patch.

p.patch-header-lead: The header fields (the order is fixed, all of them are mandatory):

tr.td: the intervention id matching `idPattern`, e.g. `# id: CK-workbench-001`

OPTIONAL (the default is `patch`; added in M1 - before the format was frozen): the carrier of the layer for entry-module patches, which the former header did not have; the allowed values are `patch`, `entry-module`, `rewrite-rule` (the last one only on patches GENERATED by the rule engine, post-MVP: the inventory attributes them to the rewrite-rule layer)
one line: what the intervention is for
a link to an issue; `none` when there is none
the upstream commit of the last adaptation
the pin at which the patch is current, e.g. `# pin: 1.135.0@08d4889f9ec4a1685d257b9b95de036c8e1ce1e5`
the ids of the covering tests, comma-separated

p.patch-body-lead: **The body** is a normalized unified diff of exactly one file:

facts.PB-ONE-FILE-HEADERS: exactly one pair of headers `--- a/<path>` and `+++ b/<path>` with the same `<path>` (LF line endings, no tabs and no quotes; paths with spaces are not escaped - there are none in the upstream tree, and their presence is an encoder error);
facts.PB-U3-HUNKS: then the hunks `@@ -l,c +l,c @@` with a context of exactly 3 lines (`-U3`); refined by the M0 implementation: git omits the `,1` of single-line ranges and adds a section heading after the second `@@` - both forms are accepted and preserved byte for byte (otherwise double regeneration is unreachable); an empty context line may arrive without the leading space - it is accepted and reproduced verbatim;
facts.PB-NO-VOLATILE-HEADERS: no `diff --git`, `index` or `mode` lines, no dates, authors or series numbers: they are not needed for applying and they carry non-deterministic data;
facts.PB-BYTES-VERBATIM: the content of the lines is byte for byte as in the files (LF; trailing spaces are preserved); the file ends with an LF; the marker `\ No newline at end of file` is allowed by the rules of unified diff.

p.PATCH-IS-STATE-NOT-INCREMENT: A patch always describes a **state**, «the file at the pin → our state of the file», not an increment. There is no order and no dependency between patches (one file is one patch by construction); the order of applying under `load` is the lexicographic sort of the patch file names by UTF-8 bytes (it is needed only for the determinism of the branch).

p.ADD-FILE-PATCH: **An add-file patch** (a new file in the upstream zone - allowed only as an exception, PROP-005 §9): `--- /dev/null`, `+++ b/<path>`, one hunk `@@ -0,0 +1,N @@`. **Deleting an upstream file by a patch is forbidden** (`--- a/… +++ /dev/null` is a validation error; hide plus the removed registry are used instead).

p.patch-valid-sample: A valid sample in full (ours, written from scratch; the path and the context lines are notional and show the form only; a real patch carries the bytes of a real upstream file):

patch-file.fence:
# codkit-patch: 2 # id: CK-workbench-001 # type: hook # category: follow # owner: workbench-core # reason: mount point for patchset center-area host initialization # link: none # cause: none # pin: 1.135.0@08d4889f9ec4a1685d257b9b95de036c8e1ce1e5 # contract-tests: none --- a/src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/example/examplePart.ts +++ b/src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/example/examplePart.ts @@ -110,6 +110,9 @@ }
protected createExampleArea(parent: HTMLElement): void { + // codkit:begin CK-workbench-001 + // (hook body lives in patchset own code; this block only delegates) + // codkit:end CK-workbench-001 this.doCreateExampleArea(parent); }

p.PATCH-INVALID-SAMPLE: An invalid sample: the same file, but the added lines stand **outside** the `codkit:begin`/`codkit:end` pair. The expected diagnostics of `codkit verify` (exit 1): `CK-E-HUNK-OUTSIDE-MARKER: delta/patches/…ckpatch: hunk at target line 113 adds lines outside any codkit marker block. Wrap the change in "// codkit:begin CK-workbench-001" … "// codkit:end CK-workbench-001".`

p.gen-io: Input: the path F, the pin bytes `pinBytes` (the git object: `git show <pin.sha>:<path>` - with no network and no checkout), the target bytes `curBytes` (the working file of the tree). Output: the bytes of the `.ckpatch` (the header preserved or updated + the new body) or «no changes».

facts.GEN-BYTE-PREDICATES: **The byte predicates** (before the diff): `curBytes` is valid UTF-8; the line endings are LF (a CR found → refusal `CK-E-CRLF`, with a hint about `core.autocrlf=false`); the trailing LF is present if it was present at the pin (lost → refusal `CK-E-EOF-NEWLINE`); the file is not binary (a NUL byte → refusal: binary targets belong to the resource-file layer). Trailing spaces are NOT cleaned up - the bytes are preserved.
facts.GEN-DIFF-INVOCATION: The diff: `git diff --no-index -U3 --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -- <tmpPin> <tmpCur>` in the isolated environment (PROP-002 §2), with the explicit `-c diff.algorithm=myers -c core.autocrlf=false -c diff.renames=false -c diff.mnemonicPrefix=false -c diff.noprefix=false`. The temporary files are created in `.codkit/tmp/` under the fixed names `a`/`b` (which do not depend on absolute paths); the `diff --git`/`index`/`old mode`/`new mode` lines are removed from the output; the `---`/`+++` headers are rewritten to the canonical path F. (The hashes of the `index` lines are thrown away: their abbreviated length depends on the number of objects in the repository - a source of non-determinism.)
facts.GEN-EMPTY-DIFF: An empty diff → the patch file is not written at all; an existing patch, once the target has returned to the pin, is deleted by the `save` command with a message.
facts.GEN-HEADER-PRESERVED: Assembling the `.ckpatch`: an existing header is preserved (regeneration changes neither the id nor the metadata; the `pin` field is updated only by the regeneration step of an upgrade cycle); for a new file the header comes from the answer of `marker new` or from the flags.
facts.GEN-BYTE-COMPARE: The comparison with the old `.ckpatch` is **byte-wise**: on a match → do not write (do not touch the mtime).

p.DOUBLE-REGEN-INVARIANT: The format requires a double regeneration to produce an empty diff. The Linux check is part of the current floor; native macOS/Windows proofs are separate open rows of the S16/PROP-013 matrix, not an implied result.
